```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(moosaic)
```

Every stage of the moosaic pipeline — reading and matrix building, detector
alignment, FID peak detection, windowing, rank estimation, the MCR-ALS fit,
identification scoring, and quantification — is controlled by `moosaic.*`
options. This vignette lists each option with its default value and explains
what it does in the pipeline.

## How options are set

All defaults live in a single place (`R/aaa-options.R`). When the package is
loaded, only options that have *not* already been set receive their defaults,
so values assigned in a project `.Rprofile` take precedence over package
defaults:

```{r rprofile, eval = FALSE}
options(
  moosaic.rank_max = 4L,
  moosaic.search_hits = 20L
)
```

Within R sessions:

- `moosaic_options()` returns the current values of all `moosaic.*` options.
- `set_moosaic_options(...)` sets one or more options by name *without* the
  `moosaic.` prefix; unknown names abort with an error of class
  `moosaic-error-unknown_option`. Previous values are returned invisibly.
- `reset_moosaic_options()` restores every option to its default, returning
  the previous values invisibly.
- Convenience setters add input checking on top: `specify_library()`,
  `specify_search_params()`, `specify_ri_calibration()`, and
  `specify_identification_penalties()`.

```{r current-options}
moosaic_options()[c("moosaic.rank_max", "moosaic.align_engine")]
old <- set_moosaic_options(rank_max = 4L)   # names without the moosaic. prefix
moosaic_options()[["moosaic.rank_max"]]
reset_moosaic_options()                     # restore all defaults
```

Most pipeline functions also accept per-call arguments that override the
corresponding option (for example `align_detectors(exp, engine = ...)`,
`estimate_rank(D, fid, methods = ..., max_rank = ...)` and
`quantify(res, info, style = ...)`), which is useful when a single run needs to
be reprocessed under different settings.

## Library and search

Options used by the identification stage (`identify_components()`) when it
searches deconvolved component spectra against NIST-format libraries through
mspepsearchr.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.library_path` | `NULL` | List of NIST library directory paths (set with `specify_library()`) |
| `moosaic.search_function` | `"identity"` | MSPepSearch mode: `"identity"`, `"simple"`, `"hybrid"`, `"neutral_loss"` |
| `moosaic.search_hits` | `10L` | Library hits retained per component query |
| `moosaic.search_threads` | `1L` | Worker threads for the search executable |
| `moosaic.ri_column_type` | `"semi-standard non-polar"` | RI scale reported by MSPepSearch: `"semi-standard non-polar"` or `"standard non-polar"` |
| `moosaic.min_match_factor` | `600` | Minimum match factor for a candidate to be kept (and for reference-peak eligibility) |
| `moosaic.ri_calibration_path` | `NULL` | Path of the ChemStation `.CAL` file used for observed RIs (set with `specify_ri_calibration()`) |
| `moosaic.ri_extrapolate` | `FALSE` | Extrapolate RIs outside the calibrated range instead of returning `NA` |

- **`moosaic.library_path`** — identification aborts with an error of class
  `missing_library` when this is unset or empty, so it must be designated
  before searching. Directories named `mainlib` and `replib` are searched in a
  single batch; each additional library gets its own search call and the
  per-query hits are merged (best match factor first).
- **`moosaic.search_function`** — selects the MSPepSearch mode: `"identity"`
  matches on exact EI mass spectra (`IdentitySearchEiNormal`), `"simple"` uses
  standard spectral similarity scoring, `"hybrid"` adds weighting/penalties
  beyond simple similarity, and `"neutral_loss"` scores agreement of the
  differences between two spectra (useful for derivative classes). The default
  is `"identity"` because deconvolution yields clean single-compound spectra,
  where exact matching is most discriminating.
- **`moosaic.search_hits`** — number of hits per query returned before scoring;
  larger values keep more marginal candidates in the ranked hit table at the
  cost of search time and report size.
- **`moosaic.search_threads`** — worker threads passed to MSPepSearch, capped
  at the number of queries searched in a batch.
- **`moosaic.ri_column_type`** — must be `"semi-standard non-polar"` (default)
  or `"standard non-polar"`. It fixes the retention-index scale on which
  MSPepSearch reports each hit's library RI, so that it is comparable with the
  observed RI computed from `moosaic.ri_calibration_path`. Set it to match the
  column type your calibration ladder was generated for.
- **`moosaic.min_match_factor`** — candidates whose NIST match factor is below
  this are dropped before scoring. The same value gates internal reference
  selection in `quantify()`: a peak must score at least this high to be
  eligible as the Polyarc reference, so raising it tightens both candidate
  filtering and reference quality simultaneously.
- **`moosaic.ri_calibration_path`** — used when no `ri_cal` argument is passed
  explicitly to `identify_components()`, `annotate_component()`, or
  `process_sample()`. When unset (and no explicit file given), observed RIs are
  `NA`: the RI penalty is zero but flagged as missing in each hit table.
- **`moosaic.ri_extrapolate`** — with `FALSE` (default), retention times
  outside the calibrated range produce `NA` RIs and a warning of class
  `ri_out_of_range`; with `TRUE`, the nearest two references at each end are
  extrapolated linearly instead.

```{r search-setup, eval = FALSE}
specify_library(c(
  "C:/NIST23/MSSEARCH/mainlib/",
  "C:/NIST23/MSSEARCH/replib/"
))
specify_search_params(type = "identity", hits = 10L, threads = 1L)
specify_ri_calibration("ONSITE.CAL")
```

## Matrix building

Options that shape the scan-by-m/z data matrix each window is fitted on.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.mz_min` | `35` | Lowest m/z bin centre retained |
| `moosaic.mz_max` | `500` | Highest m/z considered when building the matrix |
| `moosaic.mz_bin` | `1` | Bin width (m/z units) |

- **`moosaic.mz_min` / `moosaic.mz_max`** — ions outside this window are
  dropped before rank estimation and the ALS fit. Raising `mz_min` removes low
  m/z noise and solvent fragments; lowering it keeps them at the cost of extra
  columns (and, for background detection, the air-ion table is filtered by
  `mz_min`).
- **`moosaic.mz_bin`** — fractional m/z values are assigned to the nearest bin
  centre, and intensities falling in the same bin are summed. Bins are centred
  on multiples of `mz_bin` starting at `mz_min`, so with the defaults a peak at
  m/z 39.9 lands in the bin for 40. A value below one is only useful when the
  instrument's mass resolution warrants it, since the matrix columns are what
  the ALS fit decomposes.

## Detector alignment

Options used by `align_detectors()` to estimate the retention-time delay
between the FID and the MS before any windowing.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.align_engine` | `"xcorr"` | Delay engine: `"xcorr"` or `"gcalignr"` |
| `moosaic.max_delay` | `0.2` | Largest delay magnitude searched (min) |
| `moosaic.align_step` | `0.001` | Common grid spacing for cross-correlation / shift step size (min) |

- **`moosaic.align_engine`** — `"xcorr"` (default) maximises the normalised
  cross-correlation of baseline-corrected FID and TIC traces on a common grid;
  it is fast and depends only on the overall peak pattern agreeing.
  `"gcalignr"` delegates to GCalignR peak-list alignment, which models each
  detector's resolved peaks explicitly (useful when one dominant feature would
  dominate the cross-correlation); it takes minutes for dense runs, so with this
  engine the cheap xcorr estimate is additionally run as an independent
  cross-check and a warning of class `engine_disagreement` is issued if the two
  delays differ by more than one MS scan interval. If GCalignR cannot be applied
  because fewer than two peaks are detected in either trace, the package falls
  back to the xcorr result with a warning of class `engine_fallback`.
- **`moosaic.max_delay`** — search range for the delay: lags within ± this many
  minutes are examined by cross-correlation and it is passed as GCalignR's
  maximum linear shift. It must exceed the true detector delay; keep it small
  to avoid spurious correlations with peaks far apart in time.
- **`moosaic.align_step`** — spacing of the common interpolation grid (and thus
  the lag resolution) for cross-correlation, and the shift step size for the
  GCalignR engine. Finer values give a more precise sub-grid delay estimate at
  proportional computational cost; the best discrete lag is parabola-refined in
  either case.

## FID peak detection

Options used when peaks are detected on the *processed copy* of the FID trace
(`detect_fid_peaks()`). The raw FID is never modified — quantification always
integrates raw areas — so these options affect window placement and rank votes,
never measured amounts.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.fid_smooth_window` | `7L` | Savitzky–Golay smoothing window (FID points) on the detection copy |
| `moosaic.fid_baseline_method` | `"rolling_min"` | Baseline correction for the detection copy: `"rolling_min"` or `"none"` |
| `moosaic.peak_min_height_snr` | `5` | Minimum apex height, in noise multiples, for a detected peak (and FID rank vote) |

- **`moosaic.fid_smooth_window`** — length of the Savitzky–Golay window applied
  to the detection copy (cubic polynomial; must be odd and at least 3). At the
  usual 50 Hz sampling rate, 7 points is about 0.14 s. Larger windows suppress
  more noise but smear narrow peaks together or flatten them below the height
  threshold.
- **`moosaic.fid_baseline_method`** — `"rolling_min"` subtracts a baseline
  estimated by morphological opening plus moving average, which removes linear
  drift exactly and treats features narrower than the window as signal;
  `"none"` applies no correction (appropriate when `check_fid_baseline()` has
  confirmed the raw baseline is already flat).
- **`moosaic.peak_min_height_snr`** — a local maximum counts as an FID peak
  only if its apex rises at least this multiple of the robust noise estimate,
  and maxima that do not rise at least half this above their neighbouring valley
  are discarded as noise. The same threshold gates the `"fid"` rank vote inside
  each window (with a floor of 5% of the trace range), so it influences both how
  many peaks are found and how many components windows with shoulders receive.

## Deconvolution windows

Options used by `detect_fid_windows()` when detected peaks are merged into the
retention-time domains that MCR-ALS fits.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.window_padding` | `0.02` | Minutes added to each side of every peak (min) |
| `moosaic.window_merge_gap` | `0.01` | Separation at or below which padded peaks merge into one window (min) |
| `moosaic.min_scans_per_window` | `8L` | Minimum MS scans per window before a warning is issued |

- **`moosaic.window_padding`** — minutes added to each side of every detected
  peak before merging. Padding gives the fit slack for residual sub-scan
  misalignment and for shoulder mass lying just outside the detected bounds; it
  should be larger than the expected alignment error but small enough not to
  pull in neighbouring resolved peaks (those stay separate unless the padded
  intervals fall within `moosaic.window_merge_gap`).
- **`moosaic.window_merge_gap`** — two padded peaks whose intervals are
  separated by at most this many minutes are merged into a single deconvolution
  window; wider separations start a new one.
- **`moosaic.min_scans_per_window`** — windows containing fewer MS scans than
  this emit a warning of class `few_scans` but are still processed. The limit
  exists because MCR-ALS needs enough rows to support the estimated rank (plus
  the background column when enabled); very small windows are exactly where fits
  tend to be weakest, so their components carry low rank confidence in the
  reports.

## Rank estimation

Options used by `estimate_rank()`, which votes across independent methods for
the number of analyte components in each window.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.rank_methods` | `c("fid", "svd", "bic", "pa")` | Methods taking part in the rank vote |
| `moosaic.rank_max` | `6L` | Upper bound on components per window |
| `moosaic.svd_var_threshold` | `0.99` | Cumulative explained variance required by the `"svd"` vote |
| `moosaic.pa_iterations` | `50L` | Column permutations in parallel analysis (`"pa"`) |

- **`moosaic.rank_methods`** — any subset of `"fid"` (peak count on the window's
  FID trace), `"svd"` (cumulative explained variance from the singular value
  decomposition), `"bic"` (Bayesian information criterion over rank-r
  reconstructions) and `"pa"` (parallel analysis). The consensus is a majority
  vote; its confidence — the share of votes agreeing with it — travels with each
  component into the reports. Parallel analysis is by far the slowest method, so
  it runs only when at least two other methods gave usable votes that do not all
  agree; because it uses random permutations, call `set.seed()` first for
  reproducible results.
- **`moosaic.rank_max`** — no window may be fitted with more analyte components
  than this (votes above the cap are truncated); it is reduced to the smaller
  dimension of the window matrix with a message if that is less. Raise it only
  for genuinely overloaded co-elutions, since each extra component costs ALS
  iterations and identifiability.
- **`moosaic.svd_var_threshold`** — the `"svd"` vote returns the smallest number
  of singular components whose cumulative squared singular values reach this
  fraction of the total. The decomposition is uncentred, so a constant background
  counts as the first component; on noisy data the vote leans high and that is
  why it is one of several rather than the decider.
- **`moosaic.pa_iterations`** — number of column-permuted null matrices used to
  build the reference distribution for parallel analysis (the rank estimate is
  the count of leading singular values above its 95th percentile). More
  iterations tighten the reference at linear cost; fewer make the vote noisier.

## MCR-ALS fit

Options passed into `ALS::als()` when each window is resolved by constrained
non-negative alternating least squares (`fit_window()`, via
`process_window()`/`deconvolve_run()`).

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.background_component` | `TRUE` | Fit a flat background column (column bleed, air ions) alongside the analytes |
| `moosaic.als_maxiter` | `100L` | Maximum ALS iterations per window |
| `moosaic.als_thresh` | `0.001` | Relative RSS change below which iteration stops |
| `moosaic.als_unimodal` | `TRUE` | Constrain concentration profiles to be unimodal (peak-shaped) |

- **`moosaic.background_component`** — when `TRUE`, a flat background column is
  appended as the final column of every fit, so a window of estimated rank *r*
  actually fits *r* + 1 columns; that last column is exempt from the unimodality
  constraint and models constant interference (column bleed, air ions) while the
  analyte profiles remain peak-shaped. In tiny windows one degree of freedom is
  reserved for it before fitting. Set `FALSE` only when a run demonstrably has
  no such background; otherwise its signal would be forced into the analyte
  spectra and distort them.
- **`moosaic.als_maxiter`** — iteration ceiling per window. Non-convergence
  within this many iterations is reported as a warning and the best solution
  found is still returned, so raising it helps slow-to-converge windows at
  proportional cost.
- **`moosaic.als_thresh`** — alternating least squares stops when the relative
  change in residual sum of squares falls below this value. Smaller values
  converge more tightly; larger ones save iterations on already-resolved fits.
- **`moosaic.als_unimodal`** — with `TRUE` (default) each concentration profile
  is constrained to a single peak, which matches chromatographic elution and
  removes the most dangerous indeterminacies of bilinear decomposition. Set
  `FALSE` only when measured profiles are genuinely multi-modal and unimodality
  visibly distorts the fit; expect weaker identifiability in return.

## Identification scoring

Options that turn raw library hits into ranked candidate identifiers. Each
candidate's final score is its match factor minus a retention-index penalty
minus an element penalty (`final = mf − ri_penalty − element_penalty`), and
candidates are ordered by it within each component.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.ri_grace` | `10` | RI difference up to this incurs no penalty (RI units) |
| `moosaic.ri_penalty_per_unit` | `1` | Penalty per unit of RI difference beyond the grace band |
| `moosaic.element_penalties` | `c(N = 50, S = 50, Cl = 100, Br = 100, Si = 25, P = 100)` | Per-atom penalty for elements named here |
| `moosaic.allowed_elements` | `c("C", "H", "O", "N", "S")` | Elements that may appear without the default penalty |
| `moosaic.disallowed_element_penalty` | `100` | Per-atom penalty for an element in neither of the two lists above |

All five are configured together with `specify_identification_penalties()`.

- **`moosaic.ri_grace`** — differences between observed and library RI up to
  this many units are not penalised at all, absorbing normal column-to-column
  and day-to-day RI variation.
- **`moosaic.ri_penalty_per_unit`** — each unit of RI difference *beyond* the
  grace band costs this much score (so a 25-unit mismatch with the defaults
  loses `1 × (25 − 10) = 15`). Missing RIs (no calibration, or out-of-range with
  `moosaic.ri_extrapolate = FALSE`) incur zero penalty but are flagged as
  missing in each hit table so their score is recognisably RI-unverified.
- **`moosaic.element_penalties`** — named vector giving the per-atom penalty for
  elements you expect to see but would rather not: with the defaults, N and S
  cost 50 per atom, Si costs 25, and Cl, Br and P cost 100. A listed element
  incurs its own penalty even if it also appears in `moosaic.allowed_elements` —
  the explicit list takes precedence.
- **`moosaic.allowed_elements`** — elements that may occur without any default
  penalty; with the defaults C, H and O are therefore free (N and S carry their
  listed per-atom penalties because they are also in `element_penalties`). To
  make an element entirely unpenalised, remove it from `element_penalties` and
  keep it in `allowed_elements`.
- **`moosaic.disallowed_element_penalty`** — each atom of an element that is in
  *neither* list (for example F or Na with the defaults) costs this much score,
  so structurally implausible candidates are demoted regardless of spectral
  similarity.

```{r penalties-setup, eval = FALSE}
specify_identification_penalties(
  ri_grace = 10,
  ri_penalty_per_unit = 1,
  element_penalties = c(N = 50, S = 50),
  allowed_elements = c("C", "H", "O", "N", "S")
)
```

## Quantification

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `moosaic.quant_style` | `"internal"` | Polyarc style: `"internal"`, `"slope"`, `"slope_intercept"`, or `"quadratic"` |

**`moosaic.quant_style`** — the quantification model used by `quantify()` when
no `style` argument is given. With `"internal"` (default), every component's
mass is computed relative to an internal reference peak from its raw FID area,
the carbon counts and molar masses of both compounds; amounts are normalised so
that the run totals 100 wt% (`1e6 × density` µg/mL), and the reference — chosen
as the largest well-identified peak (score at least `moosaic.min_match_factor`,
not a combined peak, free of halogens/P/Si) unless you name one with
`quantify(reference_peak = ...)` — is marked `"Target"`. The external styles
(`"slope"`, `"slope_intercept"`, `"quadratic"`) instead read the calibration
targets found in the sample off their fitted curves (scaled by the dilution
factor from `sample_info()`), and scale every other peak from the nearest
preceding target of the same compound type; they use the calibration targets and
points bundled with the package.

## Setting options for a whole project

Because `.onLoad()` only fills in names that are unset, the cleanest way to pin
a project's configuration is a `.Rprofile` (or a script sourced at session
start) next to the data:

```{r project-options, eval = FALSE}
options(
  moosaic.library_path   = list("C:/NIST23/MSSEARCH/mainlib/", "C:/NIST23/MSSEARCH/replib/"),
  moosaic.ri_column_type = "semi-standard non-polar",
  moosaic.rank_max       = 4L,
  moosaic.search_hits    = 20L
)
```

Everything else can then be tuned per session with `set_moosaic_options()` or
the `specify_*` helpers and returned to the package defaults at any time with
`reset_moosaic_options()`.
